newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S.Korean October gas oil exports seen 3-5 cargoes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean October gas oil exports seen 3-5 cargoes.

text.p: South Korean spot gas oil exports for loading in October are expected to be half of the 8-10 cargoes sold in September, industry sources said on Monday.
"We don't have many cargoes for export in October because of higher domestic demand and refiners building their stocks for the winter," a Korean refiner said.
Traders said they estimated South Korea would have between three and five cargoes for export in October.
"There are one or two offers at the moment from the Koreans for loading in the second half of October," one trader said.
The offers are at about 30-40 cents per barrel above the prevailing spot Singapore prices on a free-on-board basis for 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil, traders said.
The reduction in South Korean exports was expected to support Singapore prices as regional demand, especially from China, was strong, traders said.
In addition to the spot sales, South Korea has term contracts for the export of between 10-15 cargoes of 30,000-tonnes each.

A source at Korea's largest refiner, Yukong Ltd, said the company was unlikely to export any spot cargoes in October because of the scheduled month-long maintenance of a 265,000 barrel per day (bpd) crude unit beginning on October 7.
Yukong's new 200,000 bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) is expected to reach commercial production at about the same time in early October.
The company sold three spot cargoes of about 30,000 tonnes each for loading in September.
A Hanwha Energy source said, at best, the company may have one spot cargo available for export in October.
"We need to supply more to our domestic demand for use in the power plant," the source said.
Hanwha sold two spot cargoes for loading in September, the source added.
Industry sources said only Ssangyong Oil Refining Co and Hyundai Oil Refinery Co, an unlisted unit of Hyundai Group, would have surplus product for export in October.
One trader said Hyundai might have only one cargo for sale in late October and Ssangyong two or three cargoes.
Traders said the refiners might choose to offer 0.1 percent sulphur gas oil instead of 0.5 percent if the bids were sufficiently high.
The refiners have desulphurising capacity to produce the 0.1 percent product used by Japan and South Korea.
They have already sold several 0.1 percent cargoes in the domestic market to the country's fifth refiner, LG-Caltex Oil Corp, traders said.
LG-Caltex bought two or three cargoes for loading in September and October, which were sold at about $1.00 per barrel premium on a fob South Korea basis, traders said.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3093)
